props.markdown:
Ten teeth drive thirty: three times slower. Eight teeth drive thirty-two: four times slower. Three times four makes twelve.

Each pair reverses the direction, so after two pairs both hands turn clockwise.
Turn the minute hand, and watch the gears behind the dial.

props.title: The whole clock, its dial seen through
props.textAlternative: **Text version.** The clock again, seen slightly from the side, with a clear dial. Behind it, the coral gear of 10 teeth on the minute shaft drives the yellow gear of 30; the yellow gear of 8 on the same axle drives the green gear of 32, which carries the hour hand on its tube around the minute shaft. Turning the minute hand once around moves the hour hand by one hour. A switch makes the dial opaque or clear.
